The user wants me to evaluate two AI models that solved a geometry problem.

Let $ABCDEF$ be a convex equilateral hexagon with opposite sides parallel.
Extensions of $AB, CD, EF$ form a triangle with side lengths 200, 240, 300.
Find the side length $s$ of the hexagon.

Let the triangle be $T$. Let its side lengths be $a, b, c$.
The hexagon is formed by cutting off three smaller triangles from the corners of $T$.
Let the side length of the hexagon be $s$.
The sides of the hexagon are $AB, BC, CD, DE, EF, FA$.
$AB$ is on one side of $T$, $CD$ on another, $EF$ on the third.
$BC$ is parallel to $EF$, $DE$ is parallel to $AB$, $FA$ is parallel to $CD$.
Let the triangle $T$ have sides $L_1, L_3, L_5$.
$AB \subset L_1$, $CD \subset L_3$, $EF \subset L_5$.
$BC$ connects $L_1$ and $L_3$. Since $BC \parallel EF$ (which is $L_5$), the triangle cut off at the vertex $P = L_1 \cap L_3$ is similar to $T$.
Let the side lengths of $T$ be $x, y, z$.
The side $PQ$ (length $x$) contains $PC, CD, DQ$.
$CD = s$.
$PC$ is a side of the small triangle at $P$. Since $BC \parallel QR$, $\Delta PBC \sim \Delta PQR$.
The ratio of similarity is $BC/QR = s/y$.
So $PC/PQ = s/y \implies PC = s \cdot x/y$.
Similarly, $DQ$ is a side of the small triangle at $Q$. Since $DE \parallel RP$, $\Delta QDE \sim \Delta PQR$.
The ratio of similarity is $DE/RP = s/z$.
So $DQ/PQ = s/z \implies DQ = s \cdot x/z$.
Thus $x = s \cdot x/y + s + s \cdot x/z$.
Dividing by $x$: $1 = s/y + s/x + s/z$.
$1/s = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z$.

Transcript 1 uses a formula $s = \frac{abc}{ab + bc + ca}$.
Is this the same?
$1/s = (ab + bc + ca) / abc = 1/c + 1/a + 1/b$.
Yes, it is the same.
Transcript 1 is very concise. It states the formula and calculates.

Transcript 2 derives the formula from first principles.
It explains the geometry, the similarity of the triangles, and the algebraic steps to reach $1/s = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z$.
Then it calculates the result.

Transcript 2 is a "first principles" approach. It proves the formula.
